draft.title: Describing a distribution
card: Data can be spread evenly on both sides of the middle (symmetric). Or it can bunch up on one side with a long tail on the other (skewed).
The centre is a typical value in the middle of the data, such as the median. The spread is how far apart the values are.
A cluster is a group of values close together. A gap is a stretch with no values. An outlier is a single value far from the rest.
Take 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 6, 14. Most values cluster from 2 to 6, and 14 is an outlier. There is a gap between 6 and 14.
draft.remember: Describe the shape, centre and spread, then name any clusters, gaps and outliers.

a.q: Test scores out of 40 are 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 15, 16 and 30. Which description fits best?
opts: Most scores are 12 to 16, with 30 an outlier
Scores are spread evenly from 12 to 30, with no gaps
Most scores are 13 to 30, with 12 an outlier
Scores are symmetric about 21, with no outliers
a.why: Seven scores sit close together from 12 to 16, and 30 is far from them, so it is an outlier. The values do not spread evenly, because there is a big gap between 16 and 30.
a.clue: Look for the group that sits together and the value far from it.

b.q: Ages of people on a bus in Bendigo are 10, 11, 11, 12, 12, 13, 40, 41 and 42. Which feature does this data have?
opts: Two clusters, with a gap between 13 and 40
One cluster from 10 to 13, with 40 an outlier
One cluster from 10 to 42, with no gaps
One cluster from 10 to 13, with 42 an outlier
b.why: The ages 10 to 13 form one cluster and 40 to 42 form another, with a gap from 13 to 40. The older ages are three values close together, so they are a cluster, not a single outlier.
b.clue: An outlier is one value on its own. How many values are near 40?

a.best: Most scores are 12 to 16, with 30 an outlier

b.best: Two clusters, with a gap between 13 and 40
